Thought: I need to determine the half-life of lead in bones. This is a specific scientific fact about how long it takes for half of the lead concentration in bones to be eliminated from the body.

Lead has different half-lives in different tissues of the body. In blood, the half-life is relatively short (around 30 days), but in bones, lead is stored much longer. Lead is incorporated into the bone matrix, where it can remain for decades.

Based on my knowledge, the half-life of lead in bones is approximately 20-30 years. This is why lead exposure can have long-term health effects even after the exposure has stopped, as the lead slowly releases from bone stores back into the bloodstream.

Looking at the options, D (20 years) is the closest to the correct half-life of lead in bones.
Final Answer: The half-life of lead in bones is approximately 20 years. Lead accumulates in bone tissue and is released very slowly over time, which is why it has such a long half-life in this tissue compared to other parts of the body like blood.
